units.text: Begin with the left panel. Private subnet instances send outbound traffic to an EC2 NAT instance, which needs forwarding software and a working public address and internet gateway path.
Read the configuration paragraph above the diagram. Update the private subnet route and disable source and destination checking on the forwarding instance so it can carry traffic for other hosts.
Move to the two panels on the right. Instance bandwidth, security, patching, scaling and failover remain your responsibility. Compare that operating burden with an appropriate managed NAT design.
With the original slide fully visible, test the host and both directions of the path. A route pointing at an instance does not supply managed availability or automatic scaling.
Read the first panel. A flow record summarizes observed network traffic using interface, address, port, protocol, volume, time, action and status fields. It does not contain the application payload.

Now follow the middle diagram through NAT. Interface-level address fields can reflect the observation point. Supported packet-level source and destination fields help distinguish the original packet addresses.

Move to the right panel. An accept or reject action is evidence, not a complete diagnosis. Correlate both directions with routes, security controls and application logs, remembering exclusions and missing or delayed records.

With all three panels visible, identify the network interface, field definitions and collection scope before drawing a conclusion. A flow log proves an observation at a point, not end-to-end application success.
